subject: general
question: Two times the present age of P exceeds the present age of Q by 15 years. After 9 years, twice Q’s age will be 14 years less than twice P’s age at that time. What is the present age (in years) of Q?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the second condition: 2(Q + 9) = 2(P + 9) − 14

⇒ 2Q + 18 = 2P + 18 − 14

⇒ 2P − 2Q = 14 ⇒ P − Q = 7 (The age difference is always constant)

From the first condition: 2P − Q = 15

Substitute P = Q + 7: 2(Q + 7) − Q = 15 ⇒ 2Q + 14 − Q = 15 ⇒ Q = 1 year

**∴ The correct answer is 1 year.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/046f49fcf377ad9ef74727001e7f8e600ca85a02e7efaff53c502f83e418e32c.png] 

**Given:**

Let **P** and **Q** be the present ages of P and Q respectively.

Condition 1: 2P − Q = 15 ... (i)

Condition 2: 2(Q + 9) = 2(P + 9) − 14 ... (ii)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simplifying (ii): 2Q + 18 = 2P + 18 − 14

⇒ 2Q = 2P − 14

⇒ 2P − 2Q = 14

⇒ P − Q = 7 ⇒ P = Q + 7

⇒ Substitute P in (i): 2(Q + 7) − Q = 15

⇒ 2Q + 14 − Q = 15

⇒ Q + 14 = 15

⇒ Q = 15 − 14 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1 year.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Age Difference Property

The difference between the ages of two persons remains **constant** at any point in time.

Ratio of Ages

If the ratio of ages is given at two different times, use the **cross-multiplication** method or equate the parts to find the multiplier.

Linear Equations

Age problems often lead to **simultaneous linear equations** which can be solved by substitution or elimination.</p
